purpose: P1 consistency fixture for the dsh-native Zig harness: the user aborts while the first of two tool calls is running. The started call is drained and still writes tool/result (AbortError/ABORTED); the unstarted call receives a synthetic tool/call + tool/result (AbortError/ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH); the turn ends aborted/user. Pins design B10/B22/B23 and repair.ts recovery codes.

groundTruthV4.note: Authored ACP recording of exactly this scenario: assistant message with call_wait/call_skipped, tool/call + tool/result ABORTED for the started call, synthetic tool/call + tool/result ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH for the skipped call, step/end, turn/end aborted/user. The fixture uses read instead of bash so no job/registered or job/settled events are needed.

midStreamAbortVariant.note: Variant where abort lands mid-stream: assistant/message interrupted:true with the partial stream, then step/end, then turn/end aborted/user. This fixture covers the tool-abort variant instead.

schedulerFailureVariant.note: Variant where the scheduler fails: repair.ts writes ToolOutcomeUnknownError/TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN for a started call and ToolNotStartedError/TOOL_NOT_STARTED for an unstarted call, then the turn ends error. Not part of this fixture's expected log; pinned for the P1 implementation.

schedulerConfig.note: DEFAULT_MAX_PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS=10. The scenario sets maxParallelToolCalls=1 so call_second cannot start before call_first settles; this makes the started/unstarted split deterministic. The config schema is agent-loop/src/index.ts:345-346.

scenarioInput.whenSemantics: when.kind=tool-started/callId means: after the named tool call has been dispatched and its body started, while the step is still running, apply the abort. maxParallelToolCalls=1 keeps call_second unstarted until call_first settles, so the started/unstarted split is deterministic.

rules.rule: Abort stops replenishment and drains started calls. The started call still commits a tool/result after the abort, with error AbortError/ABORTED and the canonical text 'Error: tool call aborted'.

Every model call that was not started receives an ordered synthetic tool/call followed by a tool/result with error AbortError/ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH and text 'Error: tool call aborted before dispatch'. The serialized code is ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH; the exported constant is TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH. The scenario sets maxParallelToolCalls=1 so call_second cannot start before call_first settles.

dsh 0.2.1-rc.2 does not append a synthetic abort user message. The cancellation cause is recorded only in turn/end.data.reason. Both the tool-abort and mid-stream abort snapshots end without a user/message after the abort.
step/end precedes turn/end; turn/end reason is aborted with reason.kind=user.

A scheduler internal failure drains started calls and repair writes ToolOutcomeUnknownError/TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN for started and ToolNotStartedError/TOOL_NOT_STARTED for unstarted; the turn ends error, not aborted. This fixture does not include that variant.
The assistant message committed before the abort, so it carries no interrupted flag. interrupted:true applies only when abort lands mid-stream.
The canonical abort result texts are kept verbatim; they are not normalized to placeholders.

openIssues: The task prose says a synthetic abort user message follows the tool results; dsh 0.2.1-rc.2 does not emit one (snapshots and agent.ts:369-372). This fixture follows the recorded ground truth. If the P1 harness intentionally adds one, it is a divergence that must be resolved before comparison.

The task prose names TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH; the serialized error code is ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH and the exported constant is TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH (tools/src/index.ts:487). The fixture uses the serialized code.
The P1 driver must implement abort.when.kind=tool-call; the P0 InputFile parser only knows op/text.
The Zig harness must emit sourceEventSeqs on tool/result, including the synthetic skipped call, and must not drop synthetic results after abort.
Scheduler-failure recovery (ToolOutcomeUnknownError/ToolNotStartedError, turn/end error) is documented here but not part of this fixture; it needs its own fixture if P1 implements repair.
No jq binary is installed in WSL; the JSONL check uses Python 3.14 plus a Node 24 stdin sentinel (node.exe).
